title: Product release readiness
scenario: A software team reviews a limited beta, distinguishes blocking defects from proposals, and revises a deadline.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Thanks for joining. We have the beta readiness check today, and I want to finish with a clear decision about the invitation batch. We are talking about the invite-only beta, not the public launch. Those dates have been getting mixed together in the project channel.
[00:25] Jonah: The build passed the account creation and password reset checks yesterday. We still have a problem with exports containing accented names. The export finishes, but a few names appear with replacement characters. I can reproduce that on the sample account, and I have a likely fix.
[00:51] Priya: Before we decide whether that blocks invitations, can we say who actually needs exports in the beta? Two of the five volunteer teams said their main task is downloading weekly reports. We cannot describe it as a minor cosmetic issue if it changes the names in those reports.
[01:18] Elliot: I agree. The welcome instructions currently tell everyone to try the export. I could remove that instruction, but then we would miss the feedback we specifically recruited those two teams to provide. I would prefer a short delay over changing the purpose of their session.
[01:43] Maya: That helps. Jonah, what is the realistic window for the fix and a separate check? Please separate the time you need to write it from the time Priya needs to verify it. Yesterday I heard Thursday, but I did not know which activity that referred to.
[02:09] Jonah: The code change can be ready Thursday morning. I said Thursday as though that was the complete task, which was unclear. I need someone else to test the downloaded file in two spreadsheet applications. I should not mark it finished based only on what the automated check says.
[02:36] Priya: I can test Thursday afternoon if the build reaches me by noon. If it arrives later, my next available window is Friday morning. I will check the original names against the exported file and also repeat the empty-report case, because the same code path handles that.
[03:02] Maya: Then the decision is to hold the invitation batch until the export fix passes those checks. We are not promising invitations on Thursday. Jonah owns the fix by Thursday morning; Priya owns verification after the build is available, with the windows she just described.
[03:27] Elliot: Understood. I will tell the volunteer teams that we are finishing a data accuracy check and will confirm their session time afterward. Do you want that message today, or should I wait until we know whether the fix works? I have not sent anything yet.
[03:52] Maya: Send that update today, please. Keep it factual and avoid giving them a replacement date. We have not chosen one. We can still prepare the invitation text now so that passing the check does not create another day of administrative work.
[04:15] Jonah: There is a second item: the dashboard sometimes takes four seconds to load on the large sample workspace. It is not a regression from last week, and it does load successfully. I would like to measure it during beta instead of adding a performance project before invitations.
[04:41] Priya: That is reasonable if we record the conditions. Four seconds on the large workspace does not tell us what a smaller one will do. Can the beta notes ask testers for workspace size and approximate wait time, without asking them to send actual customer records?
[05:06] Elliot: Yes. I will add those two fields to the feedback form. I can finish that today along with the update message. I will use a free-text estimate for wait time because I do not want people to think they need a stopwatch to participate.
[05:31] Maya: Agreed. We will collect performance feedback during beta. That item does not block the invitation batch. The export accuracy check does. I want those two statuses written separately so that a reader does not assume all open issues prevent the beta from starting.
[05:55] Jonah: One correction on my deadline: I just checked the deployment calendar. The test environment is reserved Thursday morning. I can finish the code Wednesday afternoon and hand the build over Thursday at noon. I cannot guarantee it will be available earlier than that.
[06:19] Priya: Noon still fits my Thursday afternoon window. Please send the build identifier in the handoff message. If the environment reservation runs late, tell me rather than leaving the testing task marked as started. Friday morning remains the fallback, not an additional promised completion time.
[06:44] Maya: Let us record Jonah's final commitment as code ready Wednesday afternoon, test build handed over Thursday at noon. That replaces the earlier Thursday morning wording. Priya's testing window stays conditional on receiving the build. Thanks for catching it while we can still correct the notes.
[07:09] Elliot: Can I also check the public launch language? The draft welcome email has a line saying this is a preview of next month's release. We have not had that release discussion, so I think that sentence may set an expectation we cannot support.
[07:33] Maya: Remove that line. We have made no public launch decision and have not selected a launch date. The beta can help us make that decision later. Please keep the invitation focused on the activities the volunteer teams are actually being asked to complete.
[07:57] Jonah: For the handoff, I will include the sample file and a brief explanation of the encoding change. I will not include any real account data. If testing finds a different export error, we will assess it rather than assuming it is covered by this fix.
[08:22] Priya: I will post the test result in the release checklist, including which spreadsheet applications I used. A pass means the agreed export cases worked. It does not certify the entire product, and I would like the checklist label to make that limit clear.
[08:46] Elliot: My list is the volunteer update today, the feedback form changes today, and removing the unsupported launch sentence from the invitation draft. I will prepare the draft but leave the invitations unsent until the export check passes and Maya confirms the batch can proceed.
[09:11] Maya: That matches my notes. We are holding invitations, collecting performance feedback during beta, and leaving the public launch date open. We have no decision on adding more volunteer teams. I will check the release checklist after Priya posts her result. Thanks, everyone; that closes this check-in.
